docs.title: Team Charter
docs.text: Team 206 strives to produce high-quality, reliable work through clear communication and consistent effort. Just as we hold products accountable for delivering on their promises without hidden gaps, we hold ourselves accountable to our deadlines, to one another, and to staying productive on what needs to get done. We value transparency in our process, surfacing challenges early rather than letting them go unspoken, along with mutual respect and a shared commitment to durability in our work, ensuring what we build holds up under scrutiny. When challenges arise, we address them openly and collaboratively, driven by a shared standard of excellence and pride in the final product we deliver.

docs.title: Product Mission Statement
docs.text: Our mission on team 206 is to design and manufacture a compact and reliable device that can sense real world input, be able to process it, and respond with a purposeful action to solve meaningful everyday problems.

docs.title: Project Objective
docs.text: This project aims to investigate and develop smart adaptive technologies, an improved user experience, better fit, improved product design, and product customization options for the next-generation AirPods. The target is to maintain global dominance in the wireless earphone market, drive up AirPod sales to 100 million+ units sold with a 60% global market share in 2021 and expand the user base more towards the luxury, professional, and fitness segments. We believe that adding smart interactions and adaptive audio filters alone will already expand our user base by 15%. With the new generation AirPods we aim to match at least the sound quality of our main competitor, the Sony WF-1000XM3, and include Active Noise Canceling that is also featured in Mifo, House of Marley, Bose, and Amazon Echo products. We will also obtain IPX4 sweat-resistant rating equal to Bose, House of Marley, and Amazon Echo earbuds, and aim to extend our range of colors, as seen in Urbanista and Jabra’s lifestyle products.

• Target group Middle-class working professionals between the age of 20 and 55. These individuals are busy hardworking individuals who have to account for every aspect of their schedules and are on a tight scedule.
  • Target purchaser Target group profile with special attention to individual pet owners.
  • Customer service Prefers low maintenance, easy to follow instructions, and easy to fix complaints.
  • Marketing & Sales division Tailor to pet owners that are in need of a solution to make sure that their pets are taken care of.
  • Retailers Prefer products that can withstand a wide range of storage conditions including variations in temperature, humidity and have a strong and compact, theft, and vandalism-proof packaging.

docs.title: User Story #1: Jenna
docs.text: Walter is a 35-year-old who works at a dog shelter throughout his day he is making sure that each dog is getting the right amount of food they need and makes sure they aren't going hungry. Between making sure the dogs have enough outside/play time, water, and aren't fighting each other sometimes checking each dog bowl can slip his mind. Now with his new automatic pet feeders that he has placed in the dog's kennels he is able to set the amount of food that each dog should get and now he can have a little bit of time to spend elsewhere. And if the feeder needs to get filled there will be a light to tell him the status of amount of food that will notify him that the feeder needs to be refilled.

docs.title: User Story #2
docs.text: Dawn is a 44-year-old teacher who has to take her 16-year-old son to school at 6:00 in the morning and just got a new Corgi puppy. She sees on the bag of dog food a dog his size gets 1 and 1/2 cups of dog food. She realizes that when she gives the full 1 and 1/2 cups the dog throws up shortly after, so she needs to break it up into portions throughout the day. The problem is to break it up through the day she would need to feed the dog at times when no one is home and sometimes when her son gets home, he will forget. But with her new dog feeder she is able to set when and how much food is released so her Corgi is able to receive food throughout the day even while she physically isn't there and has enough time to digest and not throw up.

docs.title: Aspects
docs.text:
The new product design will be based on that of the Pet Feeder with improvements based on the following requirements. The P1 - P10 is the "code" to indicate the priority of the requirement, from low to high.

  1. Producer Design
  2. 1.1 The product shall be built for the outdoor to give the option for pet owners to feed their pets outside while they are gone. (P7)
  3. 1.2 The product shall be self reliant for a week worth of food for two medium dogs. (P10)

  4. 1.3 The product shall be easy to maintain for at less 3 years of contain use. (P8)

  5. Functionality

  6. 2.1 The product shall let the user know when it is time to feed their pet. (P10)
  7. 2.2 The product shall let the user know when the pet feeder is running low or is empty on food. (P10)
  8. 2.3 The product shall let the user know when the pet's water needs changing. (P5)
  9. 2.4 The product shall let the user know when the pet feeder is running low or is empty on water. (P5)

docs.title: Meeting Coordination
docs.text:
1. The team will set reminders for upcoming meetings, and the Meeting Leader will send a reminder message a day prior and the day of the meeting.
  2. Meeting Leader will reach out to the team when organizing meetings to confirm that members can attend and will come up with an alternate time if there is a conflict with the usual meeting times.
  3. The team will aim to have face-to-face meetings, but if the teams schedule will not allow it then there will be a zoom meeting held in place of an in-person meeting.
  4. Notices for not being able to attend an in-person meeting should be given five hours prior to the meeting to give the other members time to decide whether to move meeting time, have a hybrid meeting where the member can attend via zoom, or procced without the member (Possible Exceptions: Family or Medical Emergency).

docs.title: Roles & Responsibilities
docs.text:
Appendix Table 2: Project Roles and Duties

Role Duties Meeting leader: Justin Schedules team meetings, creates and distributes an agenda for each meeting, and runs each meeting Meeting recorder: AJ Takes minutes of each team meeting, including attendance, and records action items and to whom they are assigned Assignment leader: AJ Coordinates the team's work on a given assignment to Canvas before the due date Project monitor: Donovan Tracks the team's progress relative to the project schedule (Gantt chart) and keeps team members apprised of deadlines and project status
  1. Roles will be changed every two weeks on Wednesday.
  2. The way roles will be changed will look like this, the Meeting Leader becomes Meeting Recorder and Assignment Leader, and then the person who was those two roles is now the Project Monitor then back to Meeting Leader to ensure each member will have multiple opportunities with each role.
  3. Members can inform each other either through messages or during our meetings to make sure they understand their tasks and responsibilities and assist them if they seem they need help understanding what to do.
  4. Outside of our scheduled two-week shift of team roles and someone communicates with the team they would want to change roles for the betterment of the team then that is a desicion the team can make together. If the group needs to switch roles twice due to lack of a member participating in their assigned role, then the team will have to have a discussion with the instructor.
  5. Milestones and Activities should be tracked by the Project Monitor and their main source of checking milestones will be due dates for assignments or following the teams Gantt chart to ensure they are on track with their goals.
  6. Technical Responsibilities will be decided based on members individuals strengths. If they feel confident in a task, then that member will be assigned to that certain tasks if all members are unsure then that will be assigned as a group task that all or some members can do together.

docs.title: Team Coordination & Accountablity
docs.text:
1. The team will aim to have team assignments done by 6:00 pm on the day that an assignment is due to give all members enough time to look over the assignment and make any last-minute changes prior to the due date
  2. When assignment tasks are divided this is the opportunity for the team member to voice if they need assistance or feel they are not suitable for the task if this is the case then tasks can be shifted or they can get guided assistance so that each team member will contribute equally.
  3. Feedback from the design review will be acted on by the members whose section was given feedback and will update their part with the recommended revisions. And any group feedback will be split evenly among the group to update the team's design.
  4. Missed tasks from a group member will be marked by the other members of the team and if there was plenty of time and no emergency the member will get a verbal warning. If it occurs a second time, then the group will bring this to the instructor's attention to disccus how to procced.
  5. Team members will check in prior to the assignment due date to make sure members are on track to complete their work and make sure they have a plan for completion and have a plan to get their action item done.
  6. If the team realizes a member is underperforming or givng under quality work there will need to be a disscussion with the team to brainstorm how the underperforming member can improve their work and maybe give advice or sceduling a meeting with the grader or instructor to see how they can better their work.
  7. If there are no signs of any improvement with an underperforming team member after there's been a discussion on the matter and how they can be helped and they aren't constantly making an effort to meet with the team, instructors, or graders to improve then the other team members may bring up the possibilities of a pink slip if the quality of the project would improve with the removal of said member.

docs.title: Conflict Recognition & Resolution
docs.text: 1. In the event of conflict the members should attempt to resolve it with each other by reaching out to the person they are having the problem with and discuss their issues and try to work on resolving the issue, if either this doesn't work or the member having issues is nervous to bring it to the attention of the other party then the third member can act as a mediator for the two and attempt to resolve the issue. If the conflict to still is ongoing between the two members or the conflict is between all three members and they simply can't resolve it then an instructor will be asked to be involved to see how the team can procced.
